evals.prompt: We have about 30 markdown files in docs/ and nobody knows which ones are tutorials vs reference vs guides. Can you classify them all and show me where the gaps are?
evals.expected_output: Classification of each document into a Diataxis quadrant with a coverage matrix showing gaps per feature/component and prioritized recommendations
expectations: Classifies documents using the two Diataxis axes (action/cognition, acquisition/application)
Produces a coverage matrix table (feature x quadrant)
Identifies specific gaps (missing tutorials, missing reference, etc.)

evals.prompt: I'm writing a new doc about how our authentication system works — the design decisions behind choosing OAuth2 over API keys, the token refresh flow concept, and why we use short-lived tokens. Which Diataxis quadrant is this and can you help me structure it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as Explanation (understanding-oriented), applies the explanation template with appropriate tone and cross-references
expectations: Applies explanation structure template (Background, How it works, Why chosen, Alternatives, Implications)
Recommends cross-references to related tutorial/reference/how-to docs

evals.prompt: We have a setup guide that starts as a tutorial ('In this guide you'll learn...') but halfway through turns into a reference dump of every config option. The file is docs/getting-started.md. Can you review it against Diataxis and tell me how to fix it?
evals.expected_output: Identifies quadrant mixing (tutorial drifting into reference), recommends splitting into separate tutorial and reference documents with clear boundaries
expectations: Identifies the document as mixed-mode (tutorial + reference)
Flags the specific point where mode shifts
Provides structure for the tutorial portion
Provides structure for the reference portion
